newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.

text.p: South Africa's rand retreated in the face of an advancing dollar on Monday but gained against the crosses as sterling, mark and yen came in for a pummelling from the U.S. currency.
At 1400 GMT, the rand was quoted at 4.4235/4265 against the dollar from 4.4140/4170 on Friday.
Buoyed by expectations of a further increase in U.S. interest rates, the dollar powered to 125.61 against the yen -- its highest level since February 1993.

The U.S. currency also gained against the mark to last trade at 1.7082/87 in early New York trade from around 1.6750 on Friday. Cable was last quoted at 1.6243/53 from a pre-weekend level of around 1.64.
"The rand is basically reflecting the stronger dollar," a trader said.
Interest was broad-based with both local importers, exporters and offshore players interested in buying and selling dollars.
"It's been pretty much two-way," the trader said, adding that importer demand had slightly outweighed supply on the day.
The dollar's gains against the major currencies also helped the rand to a fresh 14-month high against the yen when it touched 28.3993 -- its strongest level since February 16 last year.
Against sterling, the rand firmed to 7.1841/1934 from 7.2410/2512 on Friday and also strengthened to 0.3257/3261 marks from 0.3785/3788 marks previously.
Expectations of a further Fed tightening also triggered gains on the rand forward market, where margins fell to their lowest level in six-and-a-half months.

Traders said that after adjusting for the Fed's 25 basis point hike on March 25, the local forward market was now discounting a further 25 hike at the Federal Open Market Committee's next meeting on May 20.
One-year forward points moved to 40.85 bid -- their lowest level since September 19 last year -- translating into a rand/dollar exchange rate of around 4.83 a year from now.
On the bond market, yields were little changed as the market drifted sideways for much of the day in search of fresh direction.
The key R150 was last quoted at 15.155 percent from 15.15 percent on Friday.
"It's been very quiet with not much interest," a dealer said. "It went a bit stronger earlier but it has basically been trapped in a range."

He said that there appeared to be institutional interest to buy above the 15.16 percent, but that the market seemed loathe to strengthen in the short-term because of concerns about lingering pressure on the U.S. Treasury bond market and the continuing squeeze on the domestic money market.
"Our market is intrinsically bullish but people are a bit worried about the T-bonds and the short-term rates," he said.
South Africa's big-four banks hiked their short-term deposit rates for the first time in over a month on Monday as the shortage held steady above the 10 billion rand mark.
Three-month NCDs were quoted at 16.65 percent offered from 16.55 percent on Friday, while the 90-day BA rate was steady at between 15.95 and 16.15 percent.
The shortage was quoted at 10.674 billion rand on Saturday from 10.674 billion rand on Friday.
Bond traders said that on Tuesday the market was expected to put in a repeat of Monday's performance, sticking to its 15.10 to 15.16 percent range.
-- Paul Richardson, Johannesburg newsroom 27 11 482 1003
